_note: PRD R13. Asked after the encounter, within a window, and appended to the packet. Two things this file must not become: an engagement loop, and a survey. Every question either helps the advocate reading the packet or tells us whether the guidance was right — anything that does neither does not belong here.
intro: These questions are for the record, not for us. What you write goes into the packet a lawyer reads. Answer what you can and leave the rest — a short answer written today is worth more than a full one written next week.

questions.why: The first thing an advocate asks. It also decides which complaint route is worth anything.

questions.prompt: Roughly how long did the whole encounter last?
questions.why: The session only recorded the part the app was open for. The gap between the two is worth stating rather than leaving to be inferred.

questions.prompt: What paper, if any, did you end up with? Include any number printed on it.
questions.why: A challan or memo number is the single fastest way for anyone later to find the official record of this.

questions.prompt: Was any money handed over? If so, how much, and what were you given in return?
questions.why: Asked plainly because the answer changes which authority the complaint goes to. Nothing here is judged.

questions.prompt: Was anyone else there who saw it? A name and a number, if you have them.
questions.why: A witness contacted a week later usually remembers. One contacted in three months usually does not.

questions.prompt: Was anyone hurt? If so, has a doctor seen them?
questions.why: A medical record made close to the event is worth more than any account of it. This asks so the question is not forgotten, not so it can be recorded here.

questions.prompt: What happened that the recording would not have caught?
questions.why: Capture stops when the screen does, and nothing in the record shows a gesture or who else was standing there.

questions.prompt: Did what the app told you match what was actually happening?
choices: I did not read it at the time
questions.why: The only honest measure of whether the corpus is right. A wrong answer here is more useful to us than a right one.

questions.prompt: If it did not match, what did it get wrong?
questions.why: Goes to whoever reviews the corpus. This is how a bad scenario gets found before it reaches the next person.

questions.prompt: Did you say the suggested line out loud? If so, what happened next?
questions.why: Saying a line to an officer is the highest-risk thing this product asks of anyone. Whether it helped or made things worse is the one question no amount of review answers.
